Subject: Deployment residency — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (FinBank)

Hi Simon,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for taking the time. As promised, quick recap from today's discovery and proposed next steps so your procurement and security teams have something to react to.

Recap of requirements I heard:
- EU data residency required for PII and transaction logs (primary requirement)
- Cross-region failover acceptable but primary data must remain in EU unless explicit DR runbooks allow short-term replication
- Preference for managed option if it meets residency/SLA needs; open to Dedicated or Private for isolation and audit controls

How Redwood maps to those options (high level):
- Hosted API (EU regions): Fastest to deploy, usage-based pricing, supports EU-region-only serving. Good fit if you can accept our hosted EU region and standard encryption/KMS options.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): Same API surface, predictable throughput, stronger tenancy isolation, customer-specific billing. Can be scoped to EU-only capacity.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer-managed VPC with private control plane or on-prem package for full data residency and network isolation; good for regulated workloads and custom KMS/HSM integrations.

Open items / asks for next steps:
1) Can you confirm which FinBank teams need to review: procurement, security, or cloud/network? (I expect procurement + security + infra)
2) Are there any minimum run-of-service latency SLOs (e.g., 100ms p95) that would push you toward Dedicated vs Hosted?
3) Would the security team want a timeboxed evaluation of Hosted EU first, with Dedicated or Private as fallbacks?

I've looped in Marissa (SE) and Aditya (solutions) to answer technical and procurement questions. Marissa — can you share the regional availability matrix and a short doc that lays out networking/KMS requirements?

Next step: propose a 30-min follow-up with procurement + security next week to align on residency and procurement timeline. Are mornings CET best for you?

Thanks,

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the summary — really helpful. A few clarifying questions from security and procurement:

- Hosted EU: Which cloud regions do you operate in for EU (Frankfurt, Ireland, London)? Are requests guaranteed to stay in-region or do you have cross-region routing for availability that might replicate data outside EU in failover scenarios?
- Private/VPC: For the Private control plane option, can you outline the network egress needs and whether we can keep all control plane traffic inside our VPC (no public endpoints)?

Happy to schedule a meeting next week — mornings CET are fine. I'm looping Marta from Security and procurement@finbank.com for visibility.

Hi Simon / team,

Thanks for the questions — below are concrete answers and I've attached a short tech note + network diagram.

1) EU region availability
- We currently operate dedicated Hosted API endpoints in: eu-west-1 (Ireland), eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), and eu-west-2 (London). You can pin traffic to a single region via routing policy.
- Cross-region routing (automatic failover) is optional and off by default for Hosted customers who require strict residency — we can disable automatic cross-region replication and configure region pinning.

2) Private control plane / VPC networking
- Private deployment options: (a) VPC peering with private control plane endpoints, or (b) air-gapped on-prem package.
- For VPC peering, control-plane endpoints can be placed in your VPC using PrivateLink-style interfaces; no public-control-plane egress is required. Egress rules depend on the mode: Hosted requires outbound TLS to region endpoints; Private on VPC can be entirely private except for optional telemetry streams.

3) Compliance artifacts and timelines
- Attached: SOC2_summary.pdf (redacted), redwood-deployment-options.pdf (detailed matrix), network_diagram.png
- Typical timelines:
  - Hosted EU-only proof-of-concept: 1-2 weeks to onboard and validate (assuming standard IP allowlists and test data).
  - Dedicated capacity (reserved): 4-8 weeks depending on GPU sizing and procurement approvals.
  - Private VPC/on-prem: 8-12+ weeks depending on network and security approval cycles.

4) Cost delta (high level)
- Hosted: usage-based; quick to start, lowest up-front.
- Dedicated: monthly commit; ~2-3x Hosted unit cost but predictable.
- Private: license + deployment/support; highest up-front and operational overhead. Detailed pricing quote will follow once we know estimated monthly token/embedding volumes.

5) Latency / SLO notes
- For p95 latency targets <100ms, Dedicated in-region is recommended. Hosted EU usually meets <150ms p95 for typical prompt sizes but depends on cross-region pinning and sequence lengths.

Next steps I suggest: a short technical sync (30m) with FinBank security/infra to confirm VPC options and traffic flows, followed by a procurement discussion for timeline and pricing.

I've attached the docs requested. Please flag any additional artifacts you need (DPA, subprocessor list, encryption whitepaper).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
